It’s not comic book movie fatigue. It never was.

People were tired of a run of bad movies. That’s a quality problem, not a genre problem, and the difference matters.

Brand New Day proves it. The same crowd that spent three years declaring the genre dead is now asking how soon we get the next one. Nobody stopped caring about these characters. They stopped caring about lazy versions of them.

That’s not fatigue. That’s taste.

Was it ever fatigue for you, or just bad movies? 👇

Saw Scary Movie 6 last night, and Gregg Wayans was a standout. This was the first time I’ve seen him in a film, and I’m looking forward to watching his career continue to grow. He also did a great job introducing the movie before the screening.

My friend and I ended up enjoying it a lot more than we expected. I was laughing out loud throughout the movie, and honestly, it was just fun being in a theater sharing that experience with everyone else. There’s something special about seeing a comedy with a crowd.

Big thanks to Hollywood Confidential, Paramount Pictures, and Gregg Wayans for being there. It was cool seeing him on the panel and hearing from someone from the cast.

Scary Movie 6 is now playing in theaters. Go see it because we need more comedies like this on the big screen.

The Legend of Vox Machina Season 4 just dropped on Prime Video, and honestly, it remains one of my absolute favorite shows on Prime. 

If you aren’t tapped into this yet, they release the episodes in three episode weekly batches. The whole series is based on Critical Role which, to be completely honest, I knew nothing about before I started watching this show. 

The biggest standout here is the cast. You have an elite group of ridiculously talented voice actors like Laura Bailey and Ashley Johnson, and you can just tell how much  fun they’re having with these characters. Watching them engage live and bounce that energy around makes you feel like this is Vox Machina in real life. Massive shoutout to Collider for putting the experience together. 

Getting to watch the premiere on the big screen with other phones is a rare experience so I really appreciated the opportunity. 

If you’re completely new to Vox Machina, you’re in for a treat. The show has a PERFECT 100% Rotten Tomatoes score across all four seasons. Even if scores don’t mean everything to you, it’s a massive testament to how consistently great this series is. 

Whether you’re deep into Critical Role or you have absolutely no idea what tabletop RPGs are, you are going to love this. It’s packed with insane action, great humor, and heavy adult themes definitely not one for the kids, but a masterclass in animation storytelling. 

Go check it out on Prime Video. Let me know what you think of these photos from the event (did the absolute best I could with my iPhone), and drop your thoughts on the new episodes below.

@lvmandm9onprime @primevideo 
Thank you @collider @colliderfrosty

Spider-Noir Lets You Switch Between Authentic Black & White and True-Hue Full Color

One thing I was REALLY curious about with Spider-Noir was how Prime Video would handle the Authentic Black & White and True-Hue Full Color versions.

Turns out, you actually get to choose which version you want to watch at the start, and you can even switch between them during the episode.

That’s honestly such a cool way to handle it because the vibe completely changes depending on which version you pick.

Authentic Black & White feels gritty and classic noir.
True-Hue Full Color feels larger and more cinematic.

So now the real question is…

Which version are you watching first?
Authentic Black & White?
True-Hue Full Color?
Or are you switching back and forth?

@spidernoirprime @primevideo @amazonmgmstudios 

#SpiderNoirPrime #PrimeVideo #NicolasCage #SpiderMan #Marvel

Had to jump on this and share my Unconventional First Look at the Clayface trailer.

It’s been a minute since I’ve posted, but this one pulled me in.

I’m genuinely excited for what DC Studios is building under James Gunn, especially if this is a sign of more tonal variety across the DC Universe.

From the official description, Clayface is being positioned as a horror thriller that explores one man’s descent from rising Hollywood actor to a monster consumed by revenge, identity loss, and scientific ambition.

It’s also being framed as a story about corrupted identity, emotional collapse, and the darker side of ambition within Gotham City.

If this is the direction DC is willing to explore, especially compared to something like Superman, then we may be looking at a much more diverse and experimental shared universe than expected.

Directed by James Watkins, starring Tom Rhys Harries, Naomi Ackie, David Dencik, Max Minghella, Eddie Marsan, Nancy Carroll, and Joshua James.

Produced by James Gunn, Peter Safran, and Matt Reeves.

PlayStation needs to go portable. 

The Portal isn’t the final form, but it proves something important. I don’t always have time to sit down and play anymore. Being able to pick up and play anywhere just matters more now. 

At this point, I’d take a hybrid PS5 (or PS6). Something that works at home and on the go, even if it means lower fidelity. 

Steam Deck, Switch, even Xbox moving into handheld… the demand is already there. 

The Portal has potential, but connectivity holds it back right now. Still feels like the start of something bigger.
